acceptance: A DuckDB TPC-DI run at scale 3 or 5 produces a PASSED result with TPC_DI_RPS, full audit evidence and the owner's label.
Validator, admission and the results database refuse or demote anything without that evidence, and anything below scale 3.
Only DuckDB can run TPC-DI; nothing is published.
context: Step of the TPC-DI plan based on shannon-barrow/databricks-tpc-di. The full plan (inventory of the project, the 34 departures from the specification with file and line, target architecture, step list) is the description of tpcdi-plan-databricks-base-20261121; every owner decision is quoted on tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120. Read both before starting. Item ids keep the number they were created with; the step number in the title is the order. File paths and line numbers in the plan were read on 2026-11-21 and must be re-read before editing.
description:
## Problem
BenchBox has no TPC-DI metric and its results carry no TPC-DI evidence. Until this step every entry point refuses.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- Label, exactly: "Derived from TPC-DI. Not an audited TPC result; not comparable to TPC Benchmark Results." (CLI, result, site).
- 2026-11-21, names approved: result block `benchmark.tpcdi` with `source.provider = "digen"`, `audit.engine = "sut"` (or `"duckdb-export"` for DataFrame mode), `etl.base = "databricks-tpc-di@8e0f944"`; timed rows `TDI_HISTORICAL`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_1`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_2`; JVM options override `BENCHBOX_TPCDI_JAVA_OPTS`. "If an existing BenchBox convention requires a different spelling, the implementer uses it and lists the change in the pull request."
- 2026-11-21, scale: keep smallest publishable 3 and default 5 (list 3, 5, 10, 100). Below 3: "The run is allowed; the result is marked not validated with the reason, and publication and the validator refuse it."
- Below-floor reason text: "Scale factor {sf} is below {floor}, the smallest TPC-DI scale factor BenchBox validates."
- 2026-11-21: "TPC-DI runs once per invocation. --iterations above 1 and warm-up runs are not supported."
- 2026-11-20: "No compliance class for TPC-DI, plus a rule that TPC-DI never counts as 'official' in the results database." and "A single-platform TPC-DI cohort may be published as a documented shallow cohort ... The seed workflow regains TPC-DI cells only for platforms that pass the audit."
- 2026-11-20: status becomes `experimental`. "No TPC-DI run is published until a DuckDB run passes the full audit."
- 2026-11-21, PDGF use clause: "I rule now that publishing BenchBox results is research use. Publication needs only the full audit pass and my approval."

## Change
Add `core/tpcdi/metric.py` (Clauses 7.5 and 7.6.1): throughputs from DIGen's row counts and the monotonic phase times rounded up to 0.1 second, each incremental time floored at 1800 seconds, TPC_DI_RPS the truncated geometric mean of the historical throughput and the smaller incremental throughput. Result schema takes the next minor version, with the generated JSON schema regenerated, and a `benchmark.tpcdi` block: source (provider, tools SHA-256, report and staging manifest hashes, Java version, licence notice shown), answer-key corrections, ETL (base, dialect, SQL hash, strategies, departures kept), audit (engine, SQL hash, substitutions, modifications, tests total and OK, failed names), timing (monotonic and completion-record times), visibility executions, validity, the under-1800-second flag, the label. A run is PASSED only if: every audit test is OK, both updates are within 3600 seconds, visibility evidence is complete, the staging manifest is unchanged and the scale is at least 3; below 3 the run completes as not validated with the owner's reason. Validator and publish admission require the block and all of the above for `tpcdi`, and refuse scale below 3. The results database never treats a TPC-DI row as official (`database.py`, where a missing class reads as official today). `validate_corpus` primary metric and the documented shallow cohort; the explorer read model check. Registry: status `experimental`, default scale 5, list 3, 5, 10, 100. The run gate opens for DuckDB only; iterations above 1 and warm-up are refused with the owner's message; step 1's blanket refusal is replaced by the evidence rule. The label is printed and stored.

## Decision gates
Any field name not in the approved list is shown to the owner. The schema minor version number and the cohort key format (`3` or `3.0`) follow existing convention and are stated in the pull request. No result is published by this pull request.

## Verification rubric
Pass: metric unit tests on worked examples, including an update under 1800 seconds; `uv run -- python -m benchbox.core.results.bundle_json_schema --check`; validator and admission tests: missing block, failed audit, missing visibility, update over 3600 seconds, changed staging, scale 1 refused, scale 3 accepted; a results-database test that a TPC-DI row is never official; `--iterations 2` and warm-up refused with the exact message; through `make heavy-run`, `benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark tpcdi --scale 3 --phases generate,load,power` and the same at scale 5 produce PASSED results with tpc_di_rps and the label verbatim; `scripts/validate_submission.py --require-manifest` accepts the staged bundle and rejects a copy with the audit status altered; a scale 1 run completes as not validated with the reason; another platform is refused; `make pr-preflight` passes; the soundness review of the head is a success.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has not already chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) is shown to the owner before it is committed.
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. One pull request for this item, merged before the next item starts.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
- Sources. SQL derived from the Databricks project (`src/incremental_batches/**` at commit 8e0f944, treated as MIT on the owner's instruction) may be committed only after the provenance step has merged, only under `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/`, with every file listed in `PROVENANCE.json` and with all comments removed.
- TPC and bankmark files (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration, EULA, appendix SQL) come only from the official archive the owner supplies, are committed unmodified and only in the directories named in the tools step. Never copy from the Databricks project or the DuckDB implementation: their copies of the tools or the tools zip, DIGen output, generated reference files, audit snapshots, their copy or rewrite of the appendix SQL, or any generator code (`src/tools/**`). Never commit DIGen output.
- The specification wins over the Databricks project without asking. Each behaviour of the project that is kept and each change made to follow the specification is one row in `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/DEPARTURES.yaml`, which the owner approves at the milestone stop.
- A difference from the DuckDB implementation (djouallah/tpcdi) that is not in the written list of expected differences is a finding: it is triaged and listed in the pull request before the step is armed.
- Staging files produced by DIGen are never edited. The official audit, validation and visibility SQL is never edited in the repository.
